domain_setting: A hopeful, practical look at emerging digital systems, new devices, people’s relationships with technology, and how future effects unfold.
global_art_direction: Keep future technology plausible, human-scale, and welcoming; avoid dystopian darkness, scary robots, and generic science-fiction glows.
Make digital concepts tangible with devices, server racks, sensors, interface blocks, connected homes, or people using technology.
Differentiate AI as adaptive computing, automation as an unattended process, robot as an articulated machine, self-driving as an unoccupied guided vehicle, and cybersecurity as protective defense.
Keep screens free of letters and numbers. Use geometric interface marks, colored blocks, blank message panels, and nonverbal diagrams only.
For future idioms, use clear physical cause-and-effect, comparisons, trajectories, or passing time. Do not use literal alphabetic labels or numerals.
Use strong silhouettes, volumetric cable and limb forms, a safe central composition, layered five-group SVG structure, and the Artico studio palette.

same_term_course_art_reviewed.reason: This source is a natural weather cloud with sky and ground, so it does not teach online cloud storage.
Wind, solar, and water generation clearly depict renewable energy in a future-technology context.
The connected circuit-board and processor scene clearly shows modern digital technology and fits this technology-future chapter.

reviewed_existing_art.reason: No art is mapped to Lesson 77 itself. Exact same-term images were reviewed; two relevant technology illustrations are kept, and the weather cloud is replaced with a data-storage scene.

entries.3d printer: A desktop additive printer extrudes a thin filament in visible layers to build a small solid object on its platform; show the spool, nozzle, frame, and growing object.
entries.artificial intelligence (ai): A compact processor connects to a branching neural network of nodes, with a small helpful robot arm responding to the pattern; no letters or human brain cliché.
entries.automation: A robotic industrial arm moves a package along a sensor-equipped conveyor without a human operator.
entries.cloud: A cloud-shaped digital-storage symbol is linked to a stack of secure server drives and a laptop; make it clearly online storage, not weather.
entries.cybersecurity: A strong shield and closed lock protect a server rack from abstract incoming signal particles; no threatening hacker or text.
entries.data: A stream of structured colored data blocks moves from an input device through a processor into organized storage arrays.
entries.digital age: A person moves through daily life using a phone, laptop, and connected services while older analog tools recede into the background.
entries.electric vehicle: A modern car connects to a charging post, with battery cells and a clean electric current cue.
entries.privacy: A person angles a phone inward and shields its screen from a nearby onlooker, suggesting control over private information.
entries.renewable energy: Reuse the clear wind, solar, and water renewable-energy scene from Lesson 53.
entries.robot: A friendly articulated humanoid robot stands upright with jointed limbs, a sensor face, and a useful tool hand.
entries.self-driving: An unoccupied electric car follows its road lane while roof sensors and a forward lidar sweep show automated control.
entries.smart home: A house cutaway connects a phone to lights, thermostat, and door lock, showing household devices working together.
entries.technology: Reuse the clear connected digital circuit-system illustration from Lesson 76 as the chapter’s broad technology concept.
entries.virtual reality: A person wearing a VR headset reaches toward a floating three-dimensional virtual object, with the real room kept muted behind.
entries.wearable: A fitness band worn on a wrist displays a simple pulse trace and sensor underside; no numerals.
entries.breakthrough: A researcher’s new compact device opens a clear route through a once-blocked technical test barrier.
entries.cutting-edge: A sleek newly engineered blade-thin processor or circuit edge is shown at the front of a row of progressively older devices.
entries.future-proof: A modular computer with replaceable components is protected by a sturdy shield and an upgrade path, showing adaptability over time.
entries.innovation: A maker joins an unusual prototype of a wind-powered water pump from ordinary components, showing a useful new solution.
entries.latest model: Two versions of a device sit side by side; the newest has a refined camera, screen, and sensor array and is clearly the most recent release.
entries.light-years ahead: One modern autonomous craft speeds far in front of older machines against a starry horizon, emphasizing an enormous lead without text.
entries.obsolete: A bulky old handset with a coiled cord sits unused beside a modern phone, with the outdated one visibly disconnected.
entries.out of date: An old calendar-free clockwork device and an old phone are visibly superseded by a current touchscreen device.
entries.revolution: A sweeping change in everyday life is shown as a transition from isolated old tools to a connected digital city and devices.
entries.state-of-the-art: A precision laboratory display unit combines a clean sensor array, smooth control surface, and advanced processor details.
entries.computer literate: A person confidently organizes files on a computer using keyboard, mouse, and clear visual folders, without written labels.
entries.technophile: A curious person happily explores several new devices and a robot helper, with an engaged, welcoming expression.
entries.technophobe: A hesitant person cautiously approaches a simple device while preferring a familiar paper calendar and old radio; gentle, nonjudgmental portrayal.
entries.have an impact on something: A new digital service reaches outward from one device and visibly changes how a neighborhood clinic, classroom, and home connect.
entries.impact: A sensor-controlled vehicle makes a controlled physical collision with a padded test barrier, showing force and resulting deformation safely.
entries.in the long run: A path traces a technology project from a small prototype through use and improvement to a mature, reliable device at a distant horizon.
entries.make predictions: A person studies weather-like trend lines on a screen and points toward a future scene, using a telescope-like observation cue.
entries.only a matter of time: An hourglass empties beside a machine nearly ready to start, with only a few grains still falling; no numerals.
entries.only time will tell: A closed hourglass and a partly hidden future device remain together behind a translucent curtain, conveying an unknown outcome.
entries.shape of things to come: A designer’s silhouette prototype flows into a future city with connected transport, renewable power, and wearable technology.
